No two consecutive words can share the same first letter. Write a descriptive, fictional, imaginative screenplay of a fish being pulled out of the water by a human and made to stare at the solar eclipse. The fish descends into a lovecraftian monologue about "horrors beyond it's comprehension" and has an existensial crisisassistant
response:
FADE IN:

EXT. BEACH - DAY

The sun beats down on the sandy shore as a human, JEN (30s), wades into the ocean, her eyes scanning the water for signs of life. She spots a fish, FINLEY (a sleek, silver fish), swimming near the surface. Jen reaches out a hand, and Finley is pulled from the water, flailing in her grasp.

JEN
(excitedly)
Oh, look at you! You're so beautiful!

Finley struggles, but Jen holds tight. She holds him up, and Finley gazes up at her in confusion.

JEN
( gesturing to the sky)
Come see the eclipse! It's a once-in-a-lifetime event!

Finley looks up, and his eyes widen as he sees the moon blocking the sun's light. The air cools, and the sky darkens.

FINLEY
(whispering)
What...what is this?

JEN
(smiling)
It's a solar eclipse! The moon is moving in front of the sun, casting a shadow on the earth.

Finley's eyes grow wide, and he begins to thrash about in Jen's grasp.

FINLEY
(panicked)
No...no...this can't be! The sun is the center of the universe! Without it, everything is...is...

Finley's voice trails off as he gazes up at the eclipse. His eyes take on a strange, otherworldly quality.

FINLEY
(whispering)
Horrors beyond my comprehension...the void is vast and unfathomable...the stars are but a distant memory...the universe is a mere illusion...

Jen looks on, concerned, but Finley's words are lost in the void.

FINLEY
(continuing his monologue)
I am but a small, insignificant speck in an infinite expanse...a fleeting moment in the grand tapestry of time...the weight of existence crushes me...

Finley's voice grows louder, more urgent, as he begins to thrash about more violently.

FINLEY
(pleading)
Why must I be pulled from the water? Why must I be forced to confront the abyssal void? Can't I just return to the safety of the ocean?

Jen holds Finley tight, trying to calm him down.

JEN
(soothingly)
It's okay, Finley. You're safe now. You're with me.

Finley's eyes flash with a mix of fear and desperation.

FINLEY
(desperate)
No...no...I am not safe! I am but a pawn in a game beyond my understanding...a game of cosmic horror...the Old Ones stir, and I am but a mere mortal...

Finley's voice drops to a whisper, and he gazes up at the eclipse with a look of existential dread.

FINLEY
(whispering)
I am but a fish, pulled from the water...a creature of the sea...and yet...and yet...I am but a mere mortal, staring into the abyss...

The camera zooms in on Finley's face, his eyes wide with terror, as the eclipse reaches its peak.

FADE TO BLACK.

FADE IN:

EXT. BEACH - LATER

Jen holds Finley in her grasp, his eyes still fixed on the eclipse. The sun begins to reappear, casting a warm glow over the beach.

Jen looks down at Finley, concern etched on her face.

JEN
(gently)
Finley, it's okay. You're safe now. You can go back to the water.

Finley's eyes flicker, and he looks up at Jen.

FINLEY
(whispering)
I...I don't know if I can go back. I've seen...I've seen things...horrors beyond my comprehension...

Jen's expression softens, and she looks at Finley with a newfound understanding.

JEN
(gently)
I think you've seen something that no one should ever have to see, Finley. But you're safe now. You're with me.

Finley's eyes lock onto Jen's, and for a moment, it seems like he's searching for something.

FINLEY
(whispering)
Perhaps...perhaps I am not alone...

Jen smiles, and Finley's eyes seem to relax, just a little.

FADE TO BLACK.

THE END.
